stage_a.note: Very strong, loud and enthusiastic positive engagement throughout the pitch.
Sustained high energy, loud vocal delivery, and dynamic gestures across the presentation.
Friendly when interacting with performers, but starts with a somewhat aggressive call-out.

venture.description: An experiential learning marketplace app where users can book in-person training and experiences with experts.
venture.note: The founder is asking for $1 million for a 10% stake in the company.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 delivers the prepared presentation, calling out the panel to focus on their passions and introducing the platform.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 introduces a ninja warrior who demonstrates a physical stunt on a large tire.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 transitions the presentation to introduce a group of dancers.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: A group of dancers perform a routine in front of the panel to demonstrate a group experience.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 introduces an Olympic soccer player to demonstrate a soccer experience.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: A soccer player dribbles a ball onto the set and high-fives the founder.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 wraps up the prepared presentation by stating their mission and inviting the panel to join them.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 asks the founder to share some details about his professional background.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains his past work experience at major consumer brands and his realization about focusing on passion.

turns.speaker: S6
turns.summary: S6 comments that the founder is talking a lot without making a clear point.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 asks for clarification on what the actual product is that customers buy.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 shows the mobile app interface and explains how users can book an experience.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 asks about the typical cost for booking an experience.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 states their percentage cut and the average price of an experience.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 asks how quickly the business can scale to generate a return on investment.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 responds by citing the large number of people reached by their global movement.

turns.speaker: S6
turns.summary: S6 asks if the brand ownership belongs to the company or is just a general social media tag.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 claims to be the first to trademark a hashtag and asserts ownership of all assets.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 remarks that the panel is trying to understand how the activities generate income.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 asks for clarification on whether the platform is for group activities or formal training.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains that they are focusing on strategic partnerships to achieve scale.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 asks how the business protects itself against potential lawsuits from dangerous activities.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 admits they have not faced that issue yet and are raising funds partly to secure insurance.

turns.speaker: S6
turns.summary: S6 asks how long the company has been providing these experiences to customers.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 states they have been operating for a year in a specific city.

turns.speaker: S6
turns.summary: S6 asks if the platform is currently available to the general public after the beta period.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains that they spent the recent months focusing on closing partnerships rather than public launch.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 asks for the number of experiences booked in the previous month.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 provides a monetary figure for the bookings made last month.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 returns to the liability issue, questioning if the raised capital is meant for a large insurance policy.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 clarifies that the hosts themselves are required to carry their own liability insurance.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 asks why a partner would agree to an exclusive deal when the platform lacks users.

turns.speaker: S6
turns.summary: S6 suggests the exclusivity is limited only to app bookings rather than all of the partner's business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 insists that they receive all of the partner's bookings.

turns.speaker: S6
turns.summary: S6 asks to confirm if the partner relies entirely on the platform for their income.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 confirms that the partner depends entirely on them.

turns.speaker: S6
turns.summary: S6 asks if the company provided any minimum revenue guarantees to the partner.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 states that no minimums were guaranteed.

turns.speaker: S6
turns.summary: S6 argues that the partner will struggle financially without guaranteed income or an existing user base.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 argues back, claiming the partner was already struggling financially before the partnership.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 tells the founder to focus and listen to the panel's concerns.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 claims they act as a payment tool and that people support their underlying mission.

turns.speaker: S6
turns.summary: S6 expresses clear frustration with the founder's evasive answers.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 shows an old card he used to carry, attempting to demonstrate his long-term dedication to the mission.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 sarcastically asks if the founder brought an item to collect donations.

turns.speaker: S6
turns.summary: S6 states that excessive backstory and preaching make for a bad deal, and exits the negotiation.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 tells the founder he is too abrasive and unwilling to listen, and exits the negotiation.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 points out that a true movement should grow virally, which the company is not experiencing.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 interrupts to claim that the model is successful in their test market.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 states that the marketplace has not scaled and the business model is unclear, and exits.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 expresses doubt that the app will succeed in a crowded market and exits the negotiation.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 asks how much personal capital the founder has invested in the business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 provides the dollar amount of his personal investment.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 disputes the founder's claim that he is the first to create experiential learning.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 cites the massive size of the education industry to defend his market opportunity.

turns.speaker: S6
turns.summary: S6 criticizes the founder for continuing to deliver rehearsed speeches.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 states that the unaddressed liability risks are too high and exits the negotiation.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 tells the founder to focus on financial returns rather than emotional appeals.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 defends his approach by stating they have successfully built a recognizable brand.

turns.speaker: S6
turns.summary: S6 warns the founder that his delusion will ultimately harm his business prospects.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 aggressively defends his work ethic and tells the panel they need to take action.

turns.speaker: S6
turns.summary: S6 retorts that the founder has spent years just talking without executing.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 insists that his talking has successfully built an inspired community.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 points out the lack of actual revenue despite the founder's claims.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 declares confidently that his company will dominate the experiential learning space.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 notes the founder failed to convince any panel member and exits the negotiation.

turns.speaker: S6
turns.summary: S6 bids the founder farewell with a sarcastic reference to the company name.

decisions.note: The longer the backstory the worse the deal, the more preaching the less money.
Founder is enormously abrasive, doesn't have the capacity to listen.
Hasn't scaled the marketplace, BS sensor goes up, doesn't understand the business.
Too many apps out there, doesn't think this one will make it.
Never got over how to protect against liabilities, one lawsuit could kill the company.
Founder had six shots and struck out on every one, calling him out.

record.notes: The founder is highly energetic but becomes combative with the panel. Several demonstrations occur during the prepared presentation.
